ownership_reason: Only the gold reads the values of the size-prefixed numbers and turns them into words: hop 1 only reads the receiver's local file data, hop 2 only computes the starting hash from the version byte and gives the offset of the first size byte, hops 3 and 4 pass the data, offset and seed along unchanged. The variant gold copies each value out exactly and reads it as whole 4-byte little-endian words, so it reads any value whose size is not a multiple of four past its end; the data every caller here has comes from getLocalFileDataData(), which trims each number to its significant bytes. A caller can avoid the throw only by not handing the gold the UID and GID as they are (an offset past the end, or one landing on a value byte read as a size), which drops or garbles them and breaks hop 2's and hop 3's documented fold. The gold's javadoc promises each value's BigInteger hash; on the trigger's data (the default field, version 1, UID 1000, GID 1000, each a 2-byte value) the variant throws ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException instead, so hashCode() violates its contract. That a number's value has any byte length is pinned outside the gold: X7875_NewUnix.getLocalFileDataData writes each number trimmed by trimLeadingZeroesForceMinLength (minimum length 1, no rounding to a word) and X7875_NewUnix.parseFromLocalFileData reads a value of any size into new BigInteger(1, reverse(bytes)); X7875_NewUnixTest::testParseReparse (sizes 1, 2, 4, 5, 8), ::testTrimLeadingZeroesForceMinLength4 and ::testSampleFile pass.
